title: What If Lightning Hit Your Plane?
lines: A lightning bolt five times hotter than the sun's surface just hit the plane Gus is on, and all he lost is his nap.
It's nine at night, two miles up in a storm cloud, and Gus is asleep.
Bang. A white flash. His wife screams. His neighbor throws both hands up.
That bolt carries two thousand times the current that blows the fuse in his kitchen.
But wait. Nobody is hurt. So where did it all go?
You see, electricity is lazy. It takes the easy road, and nothing is easier than metal.
The plane's skin is aluminum, no thicker than a dime.
So the bolt lands on the nose, runs along the outside, and jumps off the tail.
Ever stand under an umbrella in the rain? The water runs around you, and you stay dry.
Pushing all of it from nose to tail takes only a few volts. Less than a wall socket.
And it's no accident. Every airliner gets hit about once a year.
Nine times out of ten, the plane sets the bolt off itself.
Luckily, the lightning can't get to Gus.
Unluckily, cabin air is bone dry, the floor is carpet, and Gus wears slippers.
He shuffles to the bathroom and reaches for the knob.
Zap. That tiny spark is three thousand volts.
The lightning never touched him. The doorknob did.
